title: Death Penalty Sought for Man Who Killed Tennessee Store Owner Suresh Patel
excerpt: Prosecutors in Tennessee are seeking the death penalty against Corey Houge, charged in the fatal shootings of Indian-origin grocery store owner Suresh Patel and Bangladeshi gas station worker Shahed Rana Mohsin during a multi-county crime spree.
body:
• Corey Houge, 29, faces the death penalty for killing Shahed Rana Mohsin, three days after allegedly shooting Suresh Patel during a robbery
  • Patel, a 56-year-old Gujarat-origin grocery store owner, was killed on Aug. 20 at Ridgecrest Cellars in Jackson, Tennessee
  • Mohsin, a 36-year-old Bangladeshi immigrant, was shot at a gas station on Aug. 23 while observing Tahajjud prayer
  • A multi-agency investigation involving the FBI, ATF, and state police led to Houge's arrest after a car chase

Tennessee prosecutors are seeking the death penalty against the man charged with killing Suresh Patel, an Indian-origin grocery store owner, and Shahed Rana Mohsin, a Bangladeshi immigrant, in two separate shootings during what authorities describe as a multi-county crime spree.

Corey Houge, 29, was arraigned in Crockett County Circuit Court on Aug. 26, where 28th District Attorney General Frederick Agee announced his office would pursue the death penalty for Mohsin's killing.

"Given the severity of this senseless murder, we felt like it was the right thing to do. Don't waste any time, it is what it is, go ahead and give him notice under Tennessee law that we plan to seek the death penalty."

— Frederick Agee, 28th District Attorney General

A Crime Spree Across Two Counties

Authorities say the violence began just before 9 p.m. on Aug. 20 at Ridgecrest Cellars Wine and Spirits in Jackson, Tennessee. Houge allegedly demanded money from three employees and, after they handed it over, fired several shots at Patel before fleeing in a Buick Lucerne.

Patel, a 56-year-old man from Gujarat's Mehsana district, later died of his injuries. His 19-year-old daughter was also present at the store but escaped unhurt, according to Indian news reports.

Three days later, on Aug. 23, Houge allegedly attempted to rob the Safari Corner Market in Bells, a small town in Crockett County about 26 miles northwest of Jackson. Investigators say he shot Mohsin, 36, at approximately 2:20 a.m. while the Bangladeshi immigrant was observing Tahajjud, a late-night Islamic prayer.

Multi-Agency Manhunt

The investigation drew in multiple federal and state agencies, including the Jackson Police Department, the FBI, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Tennessee Highway Patrol, and the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation.

Surveillance footage from businesses, residences, and Flock license plate cameras in Jackson helped identify Houge as a suspect. On the afternoon of Aug. 23, officers spotted the Buick Lucerne on Lawrence Switch Road. When they attempted a traffic stop on an outstanding warrant, Houge sped away and crashed at a Burger King in Jackson. He entered the restaurant, exited through a back door, and attempted to carjack a vehicle in the parking lot before being apprehended, police said.

A gun, mask, and clothes found in his vehicle were determined to be consistent with evidence from the Ridgecrest Cellars case, according to investigators.

Charges Across Multiple Jurisdictions

Houge faces charges in both Madison and Crockett counties. In Madison County, where Patel was killed, he is charged with first-degree murder, especially aggravated robbery, and unlawful possession of a weapon as a felon. In Crockett County, he faces first-degree premeditated murder, first-degree murder in perpetration of a felony, especially aggravated robbery, four counts of employing a firearm during commission of a dangerous felony, and firearm possession as a convicted felon.

Agee noted that Houge's prior felony convictions for aggravated burglary, burglary, and theft also factored into the decision to pursue the death penalty. The U.S. Attorney's office is also reviewing the case for potential federal charges.

Community Response

Agee stressed that the shootings do not reflect the safety of the area. "This is an isolated incident. This doesn't typically happen in rural West Tennessee, particularly Crockett County, which is one of the safest counties in the state of Tennessee," he said.

Houge is being held at the Madison County Jail without bond and is scheduled to appear in Crockett County Circuit Court for a status hearing on Sept. 26. Agee's office is coordinating with 26th Judicial District Attorney General Jody Pickens and Madison County Sheriff Julian Wiser regarding the charges in Madison County.
